text: Side-scrolling grind-house beat 'em up game.  Typical revenge story, lots of blood and violence.  This game is light on story, heavy on action.  In terms of game length, it's not too long and not too short. The action is mostly non-stop and the fights are reasonably tense without being Boss fights are creative and sufficiently impressive, as they should be.  Also features Klei's trademark cartoon art style, which I personally love. The dialogue is also terrible.  Why is this in the good section?  Because you sort of expect this level of writing to go with the rest of the so I expect it's bad on purpose.  If you bought a bloody beat 'em up game expecting good dialogue and in-depth story, you've failed at more than just your purchasing decisions. Keyboard controls are difficult to manage.  I haven't played many beat 'em ups on PC, though, so maybe this is stating the obvious.  Even after remapping the keys to suit my hands, I found it difficult to play.  On the plus side, this experience motivated me to pick up a Steam Controller to continue playing the game, and with a controller the experience is As long as you know what you're getting into, you won't be disappointed.  The game isn't award-winning cinema, it's gratuitous violence for its own sake.  As long as you know that, you'll be fine. title: shank
text: KNIFE to meet you! - Annoymous THE GOOD Shank controls nicely on the gamepad (Which is what the devs want you to play this on) and feel better than the PC controls, although Shank is a spam fest either way. Button-mashing is inevitable and gameplay is repetative as the same enemies will attack you in the same ways. I never said that it wasn't fun though, as Shank pulls it off with such style that I really cannot find the gameplay boring. Sure the enemies will take a long time to kill and you will take some damage in the process but it's fair and will drop you health and extra weapons for your troubles. THE GREAT Graphically I cannot find fault with Shank's aesthetic. The character animations are smooth, the character models are functional, the backgrounds (Silhouettes) do thier job and the scenery looks pleasing at the very least. Shank seems to break up the fighting from time to time by adding in puzzle sections which flows nicely and gives players hands a rest from the constant button-mashing. Mechanics of Shank are fairly simple with not too much getting in the way of redecorating the walls with enemies intestines, and on the topic of intestines it feels like the devolpers wanted this to be more violent in parts. I expected some gruesome deaths from enemies once I got a high enough combo which makes you feel that this game is censored. We'll get to that later. THE UGLY It's later. The story is absolutely terrible and it seems that the main character, appropriately named Shank is just out to kill the Big Bad because he doesn't lke him. I played the Steam version through to the second boss fight and then downloaded the Humble Bundle 4 version (Which I got a while ago) and noticed that the cutscenes had been changed to the point where the story makes no sense. I cannot understand why Steam would censor an M rated game, but I'm not complaining. The only other real issue is the fact that this game was made for the gamepad. It says so on the intro screen and shows it by having the default controls worse than my home country's rating system. These are two seemingly petty gripes but they really ruin the experince. THE VERDICT Do you see how I've recommended this game? I've recommended it on two conditions. These follow: 1- You own a gamepad as the default and customizable controls are terrible 2- You don't care about the story/you watch the cutscenes through YouTube to grasp the story/you'll played this game on console and know the story These are the only conditions I would recommend Shank and that's a real shame because I like Shank, I possibly even love Shank, but if I'm being honest then that's my recommendation to you. title: shank 2
text: Shank 2 delightfully polishes the mechanics featured in the original Shank faithfully, but suffers from poor anti-frustration features. Checkpoints are within acceptable range in easy mode, but are incredibly scarce in hard mode. This may feel like a step-up from the original Shank, which has absolutely no checkpoints in its own hard mode, but the enemy toughness and firepower have been massively beefed up to compensate, which will make you doubt your sanity, time and time again in the same impassible first half of the level. This also means that no matter how well you do just before triggering the next checkpoint, a single poorly timed jump into a fire or into a stun-locking mob of giants will send you way back where you all started, with little room for error and health points few and far between. If you're lucky, you may find yourself at the mercy of a couple bandits brandishing automatic rifles, spraying dozens of bullets to distract you from that mob surrounding you that has already drained half your health. Oh, the bosses. How will I begin? As if the levels weren't hard enough, the boss fights are fully integrated into the levels themselves, at the very end. Which means if you exit the level to take a well deserved break at the brink of the boss fight, you can doubt your sanity once again by having to complete the level all over again! Much has to be to said about the insanely reliable health draining moves the bosses are eager to spam, but this is not the time to tell spoilers, it may be best to let everybody to learn it the hard way. But in spite of all these, there's plenty of fun to be found in the game's built-in "survival" mode. Given the game's modest playerbase however, you may struggle to find anybody playing it at any given time. Though, the option to play the mode alone is available, at the dire cost of being alone, as the game doesn't make up for the absence of another player. The unlockable playable characters are a nice fit, though I have yet to snatch exactly all of them, as one is reserved for those who (surprise!) survive the survival mode. Wish me luck. As mentioned way before, the game mechanics are true and faithful to the original title, with new moves and gimmicks to  spice up the gameplay. As far as recommending (or not) the game is concerned, this has been a tough one. While it is rife with frustrating features and merciless mobs, it has a pretty good survival game mode to make up for it, and with sheer determination and will, the levels... Can certainly be overcome. This has been brought to you by Commissar Maverick. And until next time, farewell.

title: shank 2
text: You play as Shank. No, You do not play as a knife. (Shank - Prison slang for a homemade knife) Shank is the name of our fearless protagonist. As Shank you can unlock and use various weapons that fall into two categories: Melee and ranged. You can dual-wield pistols, blast multiple enemies with a shotgun or strike fear into the hearts of your enemies with a chainsaw. There are also sections where you get your hands on a minigun and oh god is it fun to just let it rip and watch the massacre take place in front of your very eyes. You can rack up combo-chains by launching your enemies into the air, shooting them and just being creative by using your surrounding enviroment such as holes for an example. You can also pick up explosives such as grenades and molotov cocktails. The only thing bad about the game and what also makes it worse than the previous title is that there is no co-op campaign anymore. Instead of that we get a new two-player survival mode tho. The survival mode can be played and beat playing solo as well. Survival mode offers various challenges and unlockable skins that you can use in both modes: campaign and survival. To be fair then co-op would have made the campaign a bit too easy in this title so it's hardly a con but it's still less content for us since, well, co-op is still optional. I've played through the campaign 1.5 times but i would play through it again if it would have co-op in it. Let's narrow it down, shall we? +Fast, smooth and brutal gameplay +Just the right amount of gore in both gameplay and cutscenes +Awesome music that fits the game perfectly at all times +Well done voice acting and animations +Unlockables that keep you playing the game +A whole new mode: Survival -No co-op campaign

title: shellshock live
text: I rate the game ShellShock Live 4.5/5. I play it on a computer. ShellShock Live is Excellent and a worthy successor to the game on which it is clearly based; Scorched Earth. I have been searching and waiting for a modern, multiplayer replacement for Scorched Earth for years and in ShellShock Live I have finally found a worthy replacement. In short, ShellShock Live is an excellent, easy-to-learn, hard-to-master, stable, multiplayer, 2-dimensional, turn-based, tactical, artillery game featuring a wide variety of wacky weapons and difficult scenarios wherein the terrain (and thus the tactical situation) is radically changed by explosions as each player takes their turn. +Adequate graphics which provide a good sense of style (with a nifty neon aesthetic) while providing excellent clarity even if a screen is extremely small. +I have chatted with some players who said they were playing this on their phones and if this is true then this may be one of the few games that may be fun on either a computer or a phone and may allow players to compete with one another in a fair manner regardless of what type of device they are using. +This is a fairly popular game and players from around the world can be found playing at nearly all hours of the day/night. +The community is moderately friendly and fairly helpful. Oddly, an unusually high number of players seem eager to chat about politics/economics during the course of each match. +The sound is loud features nifty explosions but some explosion sounds may be too loud for many types of music if you are listening to music on media player or whatever in the background. The sound volume can be easily decreased however. +Lots of steam achievements. +Very easy to learn and amazingly intuitive controls which, on a computer make extensive use of basic mouse controls to aim and fire using an easy point and click method. Tank movement is handled entirely with the A and D keys to reposition your tank to either the left or right. +Although I have witnessed a few allegations of hacking (once in a great, great while), I seriously doubt that any hacking is actually taking place in this game. On occasion I've seen even the highest level players miss their shots completely. +This game features an amazingly wide assortment of wacky and interesting weapons to choose from, each with its own tactical benefits/downsides which the game leaves you to figure out for yourself as you play. +Extremely easy to get into and play for a while and then get out again. Connects fast, lobbies work fairly well. +This is not a pay to win game. Items in its in-game shop don't give a great deal of benefit but merely add some minor variety. +Cussing seems fairly permissible but it is not extremely common in this game. Indeed, saying just about anything in the chat appears to be permissible. There is a curse filter option in the main menu for those who want it. +The match-making lobbies for individual matches feature your steam name and the picture/avatar you chose for steam (if you've made it public). This makes it very easy to look up people who you've played/chatted with in steam and send friend requests. As a result, this game may be a great way to meet new people on steam. Just don't get so caught up in chatting that you forget to fire before the timer runs down. (Not firing during a team match is generally frowned upon because by not firing you are not helping your team to win). +/-Leveling up and upgrading your tank feels rewarding and fun (though tank upgrades really only make much of a difference after you get a whole lot of upgrades). +/-There is still a lot more that could be done with this game but the game's developers must strike a very fine line between fun and frustration while ensuring there are always a lot of players for each game mode. -The music gets boring fast and consists of various player victory songs (which are all pretty good and fun) but only 2-3 background songs. Before long I turned down the game's background music and started listening to music on media player instead. Fortunately, the game can be minimized (by pressing the windows key) and maximized again (allowing one to use a music player during the game) without causing your game to freeze up. -The singleplayer/main campaign features many training missions but are not nearly as fun, interesting or enlightening as playing against other people. This game is first and foremost, a multiplayer game. -This game can get boring and repetitive if you play it for more than a couple hours at a time. -Players are not adequately penalized for doing nasty stuff to other players (like destroying tanks on their own team). Damage to allied tanks should affect your own hit points, not the hitpoints of the allied tanks you hit (or an option for this should exist) or at least friendly fire should be capable of being turned off. Players are not penalized for working together even when they are officially on opposite teams (like if they know each other outside of the game). There are apparently very few things a player can't do to their supposed allies but of course, doing nasty things to your allies will usually cause people to quit out of the match in a hurry. Fortunately, this game does not feature very many trolling or irritating players, for the time being. Players can be kicked from individual game room lobbies but not from ongoing matches. If a player is behaving badly your only recourse is to quit out of the match yourself though this avoids the terribly irritating difficulty of potentially good players getting unjustly kicked mid-match for incorrect reasons. -There are no options governing how turns should be taken. There are no options for round-robin, least health goes first or other styles of turn-taking. -The leveling and weapon/tank upgrade systems are all a lot of fun and kept me wanting to come back for more but higher level players can usually defeat lower level players regardless. There should be an option in the match-making screen which potentially limits the level of the weapons available to players rather than just their hit points. This way low level players might actually want to play with high level players more often. Or perhaps some sort of handicap could exist to give low level players increased health/armor when fighting against high level players. As it stands, the higher your level the more you win and it's basically that simple, though the higher your level the longer it takes to level up further. Currently most lower level players won't ever want to be in the same match as a higher level player. -There are no AI characters or bots which you can add to multiplayer matches to increase the size of a match (for instance if you have just two humans and want to play a big match) and there is no human versus AI mode which multiple players can have access to at the same time.

text: This game really brings back the nostalgia from back in the early days of my gaming. I remember playing Tank on the web browser with my friends but this game adds so many different aspects compared to the free original. PROS -There is so much to explore and do in this game. You have a nice levelling up system where you level up your weapons to get a higher powered version of the weapon and every time you level up you have an upgrade tree where you can upgrade your Speed, Health/armour, damage and luck. -There are many game modes and maps to play on with friends or without either way is fun and can be challenging -Has a store where you can buy things from and when I say things I don't even know since I haven't been there yet. lol. -There are SO MANY different types of weapons on the game that have their own unique ability and you can potentially get overpowered weapons from getting supply boxes that drop from the sky. Weapons range from peer point accuracy to a ♥♥♥♥ed up barrage and radius to rapid firing machine guns and to strategic weapons as the building or digger to make a mountain or plunge your enemy into a sink hold so you can shoot at them in the hole with pin point accuracy or as I like to do it call an air strike or chuck a grenade in the hole. There are weapons that bounce everywhere and so on. There are just too many. -Has some sort of customisation with tanks -Great classic game mechanics combined with modern day ones to keep you entertained for a long time. -Has ACTUALLY GOOD MATCHMAKING IF YOU WANT. You can make a game where only a certain ranged of levels can join you or if you want to get ♥♥♥♥ed you're allowed to join higher levelled ones. -You can have 8382 ping and play this game fine as it's turn based -many different game customisation just like adding more health and changing how l Ng the turns last for. -hecktic battles with explosions bullets and death flying everywhere if you have a big battle 3v3 and up -quite a lot of replay value -community is good CONS -Honestly this could be considered game breaking. The spawns. The spawns almost decide who is going to win the game on not and can be extremely annoying as you can have the hill or height advantage as some weapons tend to bounce away from the target and go down hill. -Has customisation but not a great one. You just get to change the look of the base and head of the tank pretty much. There should be colours, strips and accessories involved or even having 2 turrets kind of like that tank.Io game but if so it's got to have a lot of consideration and thinking into it has it could break the game for tanks being op. -The aiming can be pretty off point as in you can only aim in certain directions if you catch my drift. Just think of it has a clock, it ticks to the next second every time but the clock doesn't stop in between the second. So you might not be able to hit an enemy like it has happened to me a few times. Overall good game 8/10

text: Ah, good old Colonization, or at least the remake of it. I never got the hang of the original colonization, but this has become one of my all time favorite games. The game has two phases. title: sid meier's civilization iv: colonization
text: Broken.. and it's such a shame. The 1994 original was a classic. This re-release isn't. The graphics may be a little bit fanicer but so much of the game is broken that it's virtually unplayable. Firstly, the automated and essential wagon train trade route system is now useless. You no longer tell each individual wagon train what to pick up, where to go and what to drop off. Instead you set imports and exports for each colony. This soon results in a huge list of possibile locations for possible products and the list soon gets confusing. Then, if a wagon train's ususal route gets interrupted by an enemy unit or rival nation's new colony, it forgets what it was doing and it's down to you to work it out - which can be impossible. The only solution is often to cancel all automated trade routes and start again. Also, be careful what you automate, as they zoom around the map so fast it can be hard to find them, let alone remember what orders you gave them. Secondly, everything is much more expensive yet the opportunities to make money don't balance it out. In the classic game a veteran soldier cost 2000 to train and the price stayed at that. Now it's about 3800 and goes up each time you train one. This drains your bank account in no time. To train them yourself rquires significant infrastructure to be in place, all of which costs time and money. And by the time you have such infrastruture in place, the game's AI has made your home nation's king so greedy with taxes that even a boat full of cigars will make you peanuts. Even on this easiest difficulty level this makes the game extremely difficult as you struggle to both develop AND defend your colonies. Thirdly, the game is full of bugs; ships that set sail from the west side of the map reappear on the east side of the map after visiting Europe, forcing you to send them on a huge detour if you want them on the West side of the map again. Some commodities simply don't show up in the wagon train trade route options list. Want to automate the transport of cotton from colony B to A? Tough. You can't. Forcing you to manually keep an eye on one particular wagon train to do this - which becomes next to impossible once you've got loads arriving in a certain colony at the same time. Additionally, the colony screen just looks a complicated mess and not only do the commodities barely look like what they're supposed to (cigars are tiny purple sticks in huge boxes - why not just a picture of.. erm... a cigar?) but the colony buildings are terribly sketched outlines so difficult to make sense of you find yourself hovering the mouse over each, nearly every time (and that's if the game decides to tell you!) (bugs, remember!). It's not all bad. The unit upgrades system is nice and works well, giving you the choice of what upgrade to pick and where to allocate it. You can now get treasure from just visiting native settlements where as before you had to raze a native settlement to the ground to do that. And the Europe screen is neat and clearly shows what's inbound, what's outbound, what's waiting and even lets you load different people and cargo onto different ships. Sounds simple but in the classic game you could not do this with people and had to adjust the order of people on the docks to get the desired effect. I've played the 1994 original for well over 1,000 hours but after not even 50 hours on this version I can't take it anymore and have to abandon it. I had just set up over 20 different wagon train trade routes to feed my capital colony with all that it needed. Then a rival nation founded a colony on the route these wagon trains used, forcing them to stop in their tracks and forget what they were doing - forcing me to set it ALL up again. This took hours and is just ridiculous when the old system worked so well, so efficently and was so easy to do. The game is just broken - there is no better way to describe it. Just like No Man's Sky, there are some beautiful elements here and some genuinely great gaming aspects. But so much of it is fundamentally broken that it fails to work as a cohesive whole and as such is just unplayable and not fun. Unless a re-re-release comes out soon, take my advice and stick to the original - it might be getting on a bit now, but at least it works, beautifully.
